findings.source_quote: “I first felt the adjustment in my wallet, but I consoled myself that this was only temporary.”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “nilijifichulia” with “nilijifariji” to convey that she reassured herself the change was temporary.
findings.translation_quote: “Nilianza kuhisi mabadiliko kwenye pochi zangu, lakini nilijifichulia kwamba hili lilikuwa la muda tu.”

findings.source_quote: “I am not mentally capable of handling one more duty.”
findings.suggested_fix: Use wording that conveys mental capacity, such as “Sina uwezo wa kiakili wa kushughulikia jukumu jingine.”

findings.source_quote: “I became alarmed when I heard him yawning in the middle of the night and knew that he was not sleeping.”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “yawning” as “kupiga miayo,” for example: “Nilishtuka nilipomsikia akipiga miayo katikati ya usiku na nikajua kwamba hakuwa akilala.”
findings.translation_quote: “Nilihisi wasiwasi niliposikia akinomeza katikati ya usiku na nikajua hajalala.”

findings.source_quote: “I felt like a lifeguard trying to keep a man from drowning while taking in a bit too much water myself.”
findings.suggested_fix: Render the image of the narrator herself taking on too much water, e.g. “Nilijihisi kama mwokoaji wa majini anayejaribu kumzuia mtu asizame huku nami nikimeza maji mengi kiasi.”
findings.translation_quote: “Nilijihisi kama mlinzi wa uzima akiijaribu kuzuia mtu asizame huku nikikula maji kidogo mwenyewe.”

findings.source_quote: “the victim can be misunderstood or misjudged”
findings.suggested_fix: Use a Kiswahili word for a person affected by hardship, such as “mhusika” or “aliyeathiriwa,” rather than wording that means the injured person.
findings.translation_quote: “majeruhi anaweza kuelezewa vibaya au kuhukumiwa kwa makosa.”

findings.source_quote: “Traumatic events in our plain circles tend to receive prayer, finances, and weekly budget updates.”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “traumatic events” as events causing trauma or distress, not events causing physical injury; preserve “plain circles” as the source’s community context. For example: “Matukio ya kuhuzunisha katika jumuiya zetu za Plain kwa kawaida hupata maombi, msaada wa kifedha, na taarifa za bajeti za kila wiki.”
findings.translation_quote: “Matukio ya kusababisha jeraha katika mizunguko yetu ya kawaida huwa yanapokea sala, fedha, na sasisho za bajeti kila wiki.”

findings.source_quote: “Betrayal and rejection cause stress beyond measure.”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “betrayal” as “usaliti,” not “uasi,” which means rebellion. For example: “Usaliti na kukataliwa husababisha msongo usio na kipimo.”
findings.translation_quote: “Uasi na kukataliwa husababisha msongo usio na kipimo.”

findings.source_quote: “Hearing yourself verbalize a stressful situation somehow clears brain fog and gives a clearer path forward.”
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the mistranslated verb “kunaoesha” and express that verbalizing the situation clears mental fog: “Kujisikia ukieleza kwa sauti hali yenye msongo kwa namna fulani huondoa ukungu wa akili na hutoa njia iliyo wazi zaidi ya kusonga mbele.”
findings.translation_quote: “Kujisikia ukisema kwa sauti hali yenye msongo kwa namna fulani kunaoesha ukungu wa akili na kunatoa njia wazi ya mbele.”

findings.source_quote: “Lingering stress can cause agitation, moodiness, and the desire to take control.”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “agitation” as restlessness/agitation and “moodiness” as mood changes; “kusitasita” means hesitation and does not convey agitation. For example: “Msongo unaodumu unaweza kusababisha fadhaa, mabadiliko ya hisia, na tamaa ya kuchukua udhibiti.”
findings.translation_quote: “Msongo unaodumu unaweza kusababisha kusitasita, mhemko wa haraka, na tamaa ya kuchukua udhibiti.”

findings.source_quote: “Believe ‘Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning’ (Psalm 30:5).”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the quoted Scripture faithfully into Kiswahili and localize the book name while retaining the reference number: “Amini, ‘Kilio huenda kikadumu usiku kucha, lakini furaha huja asubuhi’ (Zaburi 30:5).”
findings.translation_quote: Amini “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).

findings.source_quote: “God will make a way for you. Many times, He opens doors just when we are running out of options.”
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the changed assertion “Huona mlango ukifunguliwa” to say that God opens doors, e.g. “Mara nyingi, Yeye hufungua milango tunapokaribia kuishiwa na chaguo.”
findings.translation_quote: “Mungu atatengenezea njia kwako. Mara nyingi, Huona mlango ukifunguliwa wakati tunapokaribia kumalizika kwa chaguo.”

findings.source_quote: “And say with the Psalmist, ‘In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion’ (Psalm 71:1).”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the quoted Scripture into Kiswahili and localize the book name, preserving the reference number: “Na useme pamoja na mtunga-zaburi, ‘Ninakutumaini Wewe, Ee BWANA; usiniache nichanganyikiwe kamwe’ (Zaburi 71:1).”
findings.translation_quote: “Na sema pamoja na Mwandishi wa Zaburi, ‘In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion’ (Psalm 71:1).
